#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-notes generator (issue #282): useful, mechanical notes for every
# release path — no more "Release v$next" filler bodies.
#
# Usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]
#   version     bare X.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z
#   range_start optional git ref for the fallback range (default: the
#               newest tag other than vX.Y.Z itself)
#
# Order of preference:
#   1. the CHANGELOG.md `## <version>` section (curated per-release notes);
#   1b. (gh-1522) the curated `## Unreleased` body — the release flow moves
#      Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE TIME (never in-repo), so
#      a pending Unreleased section IS this release's notes when no
#      versioned section exists yet;
#   2. conventional commits since the previous tag, grouped
#      Features / Fixes / Maintenance, capped at 50 lines with an
#      "…and N more" line (issue #282 E4);
#   3. no commits since the previous tag (re-tag) -> a clean
#      "No changes" body, never an empty page (issue #282 E5/AC5).
set -euo pipefail

version="${1:?usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]}"
version="${version#v}"
range_start="${2:-}"

# ── 1. CHANGELOG.md section for the version ────────────────────────────────
if [ -f CHANGELOG.md ]; then
  # gh-1522 rework (PR #1526): more than one `## Unreleased` header is a
  # merge/bot artifact duplicating the curation window — the preference-1b
  # awk below stops at the FIRST header, so the second section's entries
  # would silently never ship. Fail loud instead of publishing notes that
  # dropped content (pinned by the AC5 duplicate-Unreleased test).
  unreleased_count=$(grep -c '^## Unreleased[ \t]*$' CHANGELOG.md || true)
  if [ "$unreleased_count" -gt 1 ]; then
    echo "::error::CHANGELOG.md carries $unreleased_count '## Unreleased' sections — entries past the first silently never ship; keep exactly one (gh-1522 curation convention)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  section=$(awk -v ver="$version" '
    BEGIN { esc = ver; gsub(/\./, "\\.", esc) }
    $0 ~ "^## " esc "[[:space:]]*$" { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
  # gh-1522 preference 1b: a pending curated `## Unreleased` section is
  # this release's notes (the stage-time stamper folds it under the tag's
  # generated section header).
  section=$(awk '
    /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# ── 2. conventional-commit fallback ────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -z "$range_start" ]; then
  range_start=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | grep -v -x "v$version" | head -1 || true)
fi

range="HEAD"
[ -n "$range_start" ] && range="$range_start..HEAD"
# The release-bump commit itself is noise in its own release notes.
commits=$(git log "$range" --pretty='%s' --no-merges 2>/dev/null \
  | grep -v '^chore(release):' || true)

if [ -z "$commits" ]; then
  # ── 3. re-tag: nothing changed since the previous release ───────────────
  echo "No changes since ${range_start:-the previous release}."
  exit 0
fi

cap="${RELEASE_NOTES_MAX:-50}"
feats=""; fixes=""; chores=""
shown=0
overflow=0
while IFS= read -r subject; do
  [ -n "$subject" ] || continue
  if [ "$shown" -ge "$cap" ]; then
    overflow=$((overflow + 1))
    continue
  fi
  shown=$((shown + 1))
  case "$subject" in
    feat:*|feat\(*) feats="$feats- $subject
" ;;
    fix:*|fix\(*)  fixes="$fixes- $subject
" ;;
    *)             chores="$chores- $subject
" ;;
  esac
done <<< "$commits"

echo "## What's changed"
echo
[ -n "$feats" ]  && printf '### Features\n%s\n' "$feats"
[ -n "$fixes" ]  && printf '### Fixes\n%s\n' "$fixes"
[ -n "$chores" ] && printf '### Maintenance\n%s\n' "$chores"
[ "$overflow" -gt 0 ] && printf '…and %d more\n' "$overflow"
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-1522: stamp the staged publish tree with the release version — the git
# tag is the single source of truth, the repo files carry a placeholder
# (0.0.0-dev) and are NEVER mutated by a release.
#
# Usage: stamp_staged_release.sh <stage-dir> <version>
#   <stage-dir> — the staged package tree (scripts/stage_publish_package.sh)
#   <version>   — the release version WITHOUT the leading v (1.0.550)
#
# What it stamps, in order:
#   1. pubspec.yaml `version:` in the stage — and a hard guard that the
#      staged version now EQUALS <version> (a tag/file desync fails here,
#      BEFORE the upload, never mid-publish);
#   2. CHANGELOG.md in the stage — the tag's section is generated and
#      PREPENDED (the repo file keeps its curated `## Unreleased` window;
#      pub.dev's 262144-byte cap is enforced on the STAGED file, which is
#      trimmed of its oldest sections if needed — the repo file stays
#      lossless in git, the archive tail lives in CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md).
set -euo pipefail

stage="${1:?usage: stamp_staged_release.sh <stage-dir> <version>}"
version="${2:?usage: stamp_staged_release.sh <stage-dir> <version>}"
repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

pubspec="$stage/pubspec.yaml"
changelog="$stage/CHANGELOG.md"
[ -f "$pubspec" ] || { echo "::error::staged pubspec missing: $pubspec"; exit 1; }
[ -f "$changelog" ] || { echo "::error::staged CHANGELOG missing: $changelog"; exit 1; }

# ── 1. Stamp the version ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# `sed -i.bak` + rm: BSD sed (macOS dev hosts) has no suffix-less `-i` —
# it consumes the program text as the backup suffix and dies before

version = os.environ["FA_VERSION"]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CHANGELOG size guard (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds its hard content cap — `Message from server:
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)`. v1.0.538
# died at `dart pub publish` AFTER the tag + GitHub release existed, so the
# version never reached pub.dev. The changelog is append-only by convention
# and the auto-release grows it near-daily; nothing bounded it before this
# guard.
#
# Callers (keep both wired — test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart asserts the
# wiring; gh-1522 rework):
#   - scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh — on the STAGED CHANGELOG right after
#     the tag's section is prepended (pre-upload; over-cap trims the oldest
#     staged sections and re-checks);
#   - .github/workflows/ci.yml `publish` job gate — on the repo CHANGELOG.md
#     BEFORE staging/upload, ADVISORY (gh-1522 rework, PR #1526 thread):
#     the repo file is curated-only and is not what pub packs, so an
#     over-cap repo file must ::warning::, never fail the release train —
#     the hard pre-upload gate is the stamper re-measure on the STAGED
#     changelog.
#
# Usage: check_changelog_size.sh [file] [cap_bytes]
#   file  defaults to CHANGELOG.md (the file pub packs);
#   cap   defaults to 262144 (the pub.dev cap) — strict less-than; the
#         override exists for tests.
#
# Exit 0 = under the cap. Exit 1 = missing file or size >= cap, with a
# ::error:: annotation naming the fix (archive the tail).
set -euo pipefail

file="${1:-CHANGELOG.md}"
cap="${2:-262144}"

if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
  echo "::error::check_changelog_size.sh: $file does not exist — a release without a changelog is a broken release (gh-1452)."
  exit 1
fi

size=$(wc -c < "$file")
if [ "$size" -ge "$cap" ]; then
  echo "::error::$file is $size bytes — pub.dev rejects uploads at/over the ${cap}-byte content cap (gh-1452: v1.0.538 died mid-upload). Archive older entries to CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md (keep ~30 recent versions inline) and re-run the release."
  exit 1
fi
echo "$file: $size bytes < $cap-byte cap — ok"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Lazy DRAFT create for the release train's asset-upload steps (gh-1801).
#
# The train workflows (ci.yml binaries/web-spa, build-macos.yml
# build-macos-cli/build-extension) need a release object to attach assets
# to, but the release must never go live from an upload step: `fa update`
# resolves the `latest` release and hard-fails without the SIGNED
# SHA256SUMS(.sig) (bin/self_manage.dart provenance gate), which only the
# tag-run release-provenance job can upload. This script creates the
# release as a DRAFT — nothing else:
#
#   - body = scripts/release_notes.sh output (curated `## <version>`
#     CHANGELOG section → curated `## Unreleased` → conventional commits;
#     the gh-1172 curated-notes contract), with a minimal fallback —
#     never `--generate-notes` (review threads 3/7);
#   - body carries `<!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job> -->`
#     so scripts/release_draft_guard.sh can reclaim the draft on failure
#     (review threads 4/8) — matrix legs override the identity via
#     RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (e.g. binaries-linux-x64) so a failed leg's
#     guard can never match a sibling's in-flight draft;
#   - the view→create race is tolerated (`|| true`): a sibling leg or the
#     attach path may create the release between our view and create —
#     the loser just uploads into the winner's release;
#   - it NEVER publishes and NEVER flags latest: the single publish point
#     of a tag train is release-provenance's "Upload provenance assets"
#     step (`gh release edit --draft=false --latest` after SHA256SUMS.sig
#     lands). A red provenance leaves the previous release as latest —
#     safe degradation, never a provenance-less latest (v1.0.630 window).
#
# Usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (optional leg-suffixed override),
#      GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
identity="${RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY:-run/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}/job/${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}}"

# The guard greps exactly this class — validate here so a malformed
# override fails loud instead of stamping a marker the guard could never
# match (a forever-orphaned draft).
printf '%s' "$identity" | grep -Eq '^run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$' || {
  echo "::error::RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY '$identity' does not match 'run/<id>/job/<name>' — the draft lifecycle guard could never reclaim such a draft" >&2
  exit 1
}

# Already created (by a sibling leg, the attach path, or a previous run)?
# Drafts and published releases both resolve here — upload-only is safe.
if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "release $tag already exists — lazy draft create skipped"
  exit 0
fi

# Body: curated notes (CHANGELOG section / Unreleased / conventional
# commits) plus the ownership marker the guard verifies before deleting.
# stderr is NOT swallowed: release_notes.sh's ::error gates (e.g. the
# duplicate-'## Unreleased' curation guard) must stay visible even when
# the minimal fallback below keeps the train moving.
notes_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/release-lazy-notes.XXXXXX")"

## Development Mode: Plan (plan-mode protocol appendix)

This leg runs in **plan mode**: work through an explicit, committed task
plan instead of free-form execution. Everything else in the instruction
pack still applies unchanged — this appendix only structures HOW you work.
`<KEY>` below is the current ticket key.

### 1. Decompose before editing

- Before writing any production code, break the ticket into numbered tasks
  `T1..Tn` in `outputs/<KEY>/plan.md` (the working copy).
- Every task carries exactly two fields:
  - `what` — the concrete change this task makes;
  - `verify` — how to check it passed (the command to run and the expected
    result).
- End the plan with two sections:
  - `## Decisions` — the chosen approach for every open point;
  - `## Open questions` — anything unresolved, with the workaround you picked.

### 2. Mirror the plan into a committed snapshot

- Mirror the plan to `.dmtools/plan-snapshot.md` and commit it on the dev
  branch right away: commit subject `<KEY>: plan`.
- The snapshot — not the working copy — is the durable artifact: it survives
  interruption windows and CI session-cache loss. (`outputs/` never rides
  commits.)
- When a task completes: mark its checkbox `[x]` in BOTH files and commit
  the snapshot update: `<KEY>: plan update T# done` (one commit per task).
- The periodic WIP auto-save commits keep running as usual; your plan
  commits coexist with them.

### 3. Resume rule (continuation legs)

- At leg start: if a plan file (`outputs/<KEY>/plan.md` or
  `.dmtools/plan-snapshot.md`) already exists, or the branch already carries
  commits, this leg is a CONTINUATION, not a fresh start:
  1. Read the plan and `git log`.
  2. Reconcile the plan checkboxes against the actual branch diff — a task
     whose change is already on the branch is done, checkbox or not.
  3. Execute ONLY the still-pending tasks.

### 4. Close out — the plan file never rides the pull request

- When the LAST task is done (every checkbox `[x]`), remove the snapshot
  from the branch again: `git rm .dmtools/plan-snapshot.md`, commit
  subject `<KEY>: plan done`.
- Do this BEFORE writing `outputs/<KEY>/response.md`: the completion
  report is the leg's deliverable — the plan file is leg scaffolding.
- The engine repeats this cleanup defensively before the PR is created,
  so an open pull request never carries the plan file.

def template_named_entries(repo: str) -> list:
    return [e for e in sorted(os.listdir(repo)) if "${" in e]


def check(repo: str) -> int:
    failures = []

    stray = sorted(tracked_root_entries(repo) - ALLOWED)
    if stray:
        failures.append(
            "tracked root entries outside the allow-list:\n"
            + "\n".join(f"  - {e}" for e in stray)
            + f"\n{STATE_DIR_HINT}"
        )

    tmpl = template_named_entries(repo)
    if tmpl:
        failures.append(
            "template-named root entries (unexpanded ${...}):\n"
            + "\n".join(f"  - {e}" for e in tmpl)
            + f"\n{TEMPLATE_HINT}"
        )

    if failures:
        print("root allow-list guard: FAILED\n")
        for f in failures:
            print(f)
        return 1
    print(f"root allow-list guard: ok ({len(ALLOWED)} allow-listed entries)")
    return 0


def self_test() -> int:
    """Fixture repo: clean passes; a stray file and the ${...} template
    class both fail."""
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="root-allowlist-selftest-")
    try:
        repo = os.path.join(tmp, "repo")
        os.makedirs(repo)
        git = lambda *a: subprocess.run(  # noqa: E731
            ["git", *a], cwd=repo,
            capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
        )
        git("init", "-q")
        for name, content in (("README.md", "# t\n"), ("pubspec.yaml", "name: t\n")):
            with open(os.path.join(repo, name), "w") as fh:
                fh.write(content)
        git("add", "-A")
        git("-c", "user.email=t@t", "-c", "user.name=t", "commit", "-qm", "init")
        here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
        guard = os.path.join(here, "check_root_allowlist.py")

        def run(*args):
            return subprocess.run(
                [sys.executable, guard, *args], cwd=repo,
                capture_output=True, text=True,
            )

        r = run()
        if r.returncode != 0:
            print(f"self-test: clean fixture FAILED\n{r.stdout}{r.stderr}")
            return 1

        with open(os.path.join(repo, "chat_read_cursors.json"), "w") as fh:
            fh.write("{}\n")
        git("add", "-A")
        git("-c", "user.email=t@t", "-c", "user.name=t", "commit", "-qm", "stray")
        r = run()
        if r.returncode != 1 or "chat_read_cursors.json" not in r.stdout:
            print(f"self-test: stray-file case FAILED\n{r.stdout}{r.stderr}")
            return 1

        os.makedirs(os.path.join(repo, "${Directory.systemTemp.path}"))
        r = run()
        if r.returncode != 1 or "systemTemp" not in r.stdout:
            print(f"self-test: template-entry case FAILED\n{r.stdout}{r.stderr}")
            return 1

        print("self-test: PASS (clean ok, stray fails, template class fails)")
        return 0
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--repo", default=os.getcwd(), help="repo root (default: cwd)")
    ap.add_argument("--self-test", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.self_test:
        return self_test()
    return check(args.repo)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

- CHANGELOG.md = thin GENERATED index (preamble + generated `## Unreleased`

- Release notes preference order: curated `## <version>` → NEW entries
  aggregate (flat bullets, filename order — byte-parity shape with the old

arguments.newText:
# gh-1522 preference 1c: a pending curated `## Unreleased` section is
  # this release's notes (the stage-time stamper folds it under the tag's
  # generated section header). Captured here, printed only if the NEWER
  # gh-2463 entries level (below) yields nothing.
  section=$(awk '
    /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
fi

# gh-2463 preference 1b: the pending changelog/entries aggregate. dart
# missing (or the dir absent) falls through to the legacy levels — a
# generator FAILURE with entries present is loud (notes missing an entry
# is a shipped omission, not a fallback situation).
if command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -d changelog/entries ]; then
  gen_err="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/release-notes-gen.XXXXXX")"
  gen_ok=0
  entries_section=$(dart "$script_dir/gen_changelog.dart" --stdout 2>"$gen_err") && gen_ok=1
  cat "$gen_err" >&2
  rm -f "$gen_err"
  if [ "$gen_ok" -ne 1 ]; then
    echo "::error::changelog/entries aggregation failed — refusing to produce release notes that silently drop entries (gh-2463); fix or remove the broken entry file(s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$entries_section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$entries_section"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# gh-1522 preference 1c (continued): the captured curated Unreleased body.
if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "${section:-}" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""gh-2463 — changelog entries guard.

The changelog merge surface is PER-ENTRY FILES now
(`changelog/entries/<issue-or-pr>-<slug>.md`, YAML frontmatter + 1–3
user-facing bullets; conventions: docs/agents/commits-releases.md). The
shared-file habit this card retired must not creep back, and every PR must
document its user-facing change:

  1. HARD (every event): the diff must NOT touch the generated
     CHANGELOG.md, the root CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md, or changelog/archive/**.
     CHANGELOG.md is written by scripts/gen_changelog.dart
     (--write-changelog) only; archive files move via housekeeping PRs of
     the entry owners... never by editing the archive of a different change.
  2. ENTRY REQUIREMENT: the diff must ADD at least one
     changelog/entries/*.md file. On pull_request events the `no-changelog`
     label waives this (meta/CI/test-only changes). WITHOUT PR label
     context (push/validation-dispatch arms) the requirement degrades to a
     ::warning:: — the pull_request run is the hard gate; a dispatch must
     never false-red for a label it cannot see (same fail-safe direction as
     the #1267 classifier: over-notify, never silently pass a PR arm).
  3. An EMPTY diff passes (main pushes diff to nothing via merge-base).

Usage:
  python3 scripts/check_changelog_entry.py [--base REF] [--head REF]
      [--labels CSV] [--pr-context true|false] [--self-test]
  BASE_REF/HEAD_REF env vars are honored (ci.yml wiring); the base falls
  back to merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) so push/dispatch arms diff the
  actually-landed changes.
"""
import argparse
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

ENTRY_RE = re.compile(r"^changelog/entries/\d+-[a-z0-9-]+\.md$")
FORBIDDEN = ("CHANGELOG.md", "CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md")
FORBIDDEN_PREFIX = "changelog/archive/"
NO_CHANGELOG_LABEL = "no-changelog"


def _diff_files(repo: str, base: str, head: str) -> list:
    out = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "diff", "--name-status", base, head],
        cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
    ).stdout
    files = []
    for line in out.splitlines():
        parts = line.split("\t")
        if len(parts) < 2:
            continue
        status = parts[0][0]  # A / M / D / R / C...
        for path in parts[1:]:
            if status in ("R", "C"):
                # rename/carry two paths: the destination is the live one
                continue
            files.append((status, path))
    return files


def check(repo: str, base: str | None, head: str | None, labels: str,
          pr_context: bool) -> int:
    if not base:
        base = os.environ.get("BASE_REF", "")
    if not head:
        head = os.environ.get("HEAD_REF", "")
    if not head:
        head = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=repo,
            capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
        ).stdout.strip()
    if not base:
        merged = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "merge-base", "origin/main", head], cwd=repo,
            capture_output=True, text=True,
        )
        base = merged.stdout.strip() if merged.returncode == 0 else head

    files = _diff_files(repo, base, head)
    if not files:
        print("changelog entries guard: empty diff — nothing to check")
        return 0

    failures = []
    for status, path in files:
        if path in FORBIDDEN or path.startswith(FORBIDDEN_PREFIX):
            failures.append(
                f"forbidden changelog edit ({status} {path}): CHANGELOG.md is "

def self_test() -> int:
    """Fixture repo per case: green paths + every red path."""
    def git(repo, *args):
        return subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-c", "user.email=t@t", "-c", "user.name=t", *args],
            cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True,
        )

    def fixture(name):
        repo = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="cl-guard-"), name)
        os.makedirs(repo)
        git(repo, "init", "-q", "-b", "main")
        with open(os.path.join(repo, "CHANGELOG.md"), "w") as fh:
            fh.write("# Changelog\n")
        with open(os.path.join(repo, "README.md"), "w") as fh:
            fh.write("# t\n")
        git(repo, "add", "-A")
        git(repo, "commit", "-qm", "init")
        return repo

    def entry(repo, name):
        d = os.path.join(repo, "changelog", "entries")
        os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
        with open(os.path.join(d, name), "w") as fh:
            fh.write("---\ntype: fix\nissue: %s\n---\n\n- bullet\n"
                     % name.split("-")[0])

    def run(repo, pr_context="true", labels=""):
        return subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, os.path.abspath(__file__),
             "--base", "HEAD~1", "--head", "HEAD",
             "--pr-context", pr_context, "--labels", labels],
            cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True,
        )

    cases = []

    r = run((lambda repo: (
        entry(repo, "100-fix.md"), git(repo, "add", "-A"),
        git(repo, "commit", "-qm", "x"), repo)[3])(
        fixture("entry-added")))
    cases.append(("entry added passes", r, 0))

    def edit_changelog(repo):
        entry(repo, "101-fix.md")
        with open(os.path.join(repo, "CHANGELOG.md"), "w") as fh:
            fh.write("# hand\n")
        git(repo, "add", "-A")
        git(repo, "commit", "-qm", "x")
        return repo
    r = run(edit_changelog(fixture("changelog-edit")))
    cases.append(("CHANGELOG.md edit fails", r, 1))

    def edit_archive(repo):
        d = os.path.join(repo, "changelog", "archive")
        os.makedirs(d)
        with open(os.path.join(d, "1.0.551.md"), "w") as fh:
            fh.write("## 1.0.551\n")
        git(repo, "add", "-A")
        git(repo, "commit", "-qm", "x")
        return repo
    r = run(edit_archive(fixture("archive-edit")))
    cases.append(("archive edit fails", r, 1))

    def code_only(repo):
        with open(os.path.join(repo, "lib.dart"), "w") as fh:
            fh.write("void f() {}\n")
        git(repo, "add", "-A")
        git(repo, "commit", "-qm", "x")
        return repo
    r = run(code_only(fixture("no-entry")))
    cases.append(("no entry fails on PR", r, 1))

    r = run(code_only(fixture("labeled")), labels=NO_CHANGELOG_LABEL)
    cases.append(("no-changelog label passes", r, 0))

    r = run(code_only(fixture("wrong-label")), labels="some-other")
    cases.append(("unrelated label fails", r, 1))

    r = run(code_only(fixture("dispatch")), pr_context="false")
    cases.append(("dispatch arm warns, passes", r, 0))

    repo = fixture("empty-diff")
    r = run(repo, pr_context="false")
    cases.append(("empty diff passes", r, 0))

    for name, r, want in cases:
        if r.returncode != want:
            print(f"self-test: {name} FAILED (rc={r.returncode}, "
                  f"want {want})\n{r.stdout}{r.stderr}")
            return 1
    print("self-test: PASS (entry ok, forbidden edits red, label waiver, "
          "dispatch warn-only, empty diff)")
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--base", help="base ref (default BASE_REF / merge-base)")
    ap.add_argument("--head", help="head ref (default HEAD_REF / HEAD)")
    ap.add_argument("--labels", default=os.environ.get("CHANGELOG_LABELS", ""),
                    help="comma-separated PR labels")
    ap.add_argument("--pr-context",
                    default=os.environ.get("CHANGELOG_PR_CONTEXT", "false"),
                    help="true on pull_request events (label waiver active)")
    ap.add_argument("--self-test", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.self_test:
        return self_test()
    return check(os.getcwd(), args.base, args.head, args.labels,
                 args.pr_context.strip().lower() == "true")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

  PREPENDS the tag's generated changelog section to the staged CHANGELOG

  PRs add lines under `## Unreleased`; `scripts/release_notes.sh` picks
  curated `## <version>` → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional
  commits since the previous tag. The pub.dev 262144-byte changelog cap is

5:## Commits and releases
  `daily-publish.yml` play leg dispatches `build-mobile.yml` with
  `android_content=all`, so every release train redeploys the listing.

arguments.command:
cat >> docs/agents/commits-releases.md <<'EOF'

## Changelog entries (gh-2463 — per-change files, no shared file)

- ONE Markdown file per change: `changelog/entries/<issue-or-pr>-<slug>.md`
  (numeric prefix = the sort + rework-dedupe key; slug lowercase-hyphen).
  Parallel PRs never touch a shared file, so changelog merge conflicts are
  structurally impossible.
- Entry format — YAML frontmatter + 1–3 user-facing bullet lines:

  ```
  ---
  type: feat|fix|perf|docs|ci|other   # required; `other` is the fallback
  scope: <short scope, optional>
  issue: <issue or PR number, optional>
  ---

  - the user-facing change in 1–3 lines (rides the release notes verbatim)
  ```

- Aggregation: `dart scripts/gen_changelog.dart` — `--stdout` prints the
  pending aggregate (flat bullets, entry order — the same shape the old
  curated `## Unreleased` body had), `--group-by-type` groups under type
  headings, `--validate` is the CI lint, `--write-changelog` regenerates
  the thin CHANGELOG.md index (preamble + `## Unreleased` + archive
  index). Entries sharing an `issue:` are rework duplicates: the LAST file
  wins, the loser is dropped from the notes (reported on stderr).
- Release time: `scripts/release_notes.sh` aggregates the pending entries
  into the release body; `stamp_staged_release.sh` folds them into the
  tag's `## <version>` section in the STAGED package (gh-1522 — the repo
  files are never mutated by a release). Pending entries keep
  accumulating under `## Unreleased` until the tag cuts, exactly like the
  old curated window — but per-file now, so housekeeping (moving your OWN
  consumed entry into `changelog/archive/`) is a conflict-free one-file PR.
- CHANGELOG.md is a GENERATED index: `--write-changelog` writes it, and
  the CI changelog entries guard (`scripts/check_changelog_entry.py`,
  ci.yml `static` job) rejects hand edits to it, CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md, and
  `changelog/archive/**`, and requires every PR to add an entry file (or
  carry the `no-changelog` label — pure meta/CI/test changes).
- History: `changelog/archive/<version>.md` holds one file per version
  (1.0.506–1.0.551 migrated verbatim from the old CHANGELOG.md;
  `legacy-unreleased.md` is the retired curated Unreleased body that rode
  releases 1.0.552+); the pre-1.0.506 tail stays in the root
  `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md` (gh-1452).
EOF

def _diff_files(repo: str, base: str, head: str) -> list:
    out = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "diff", "--name-status", base, head],
        cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
    ).stdout
    files = []
    for line in out.splitlines():
        parts = line.split("\t")
        if len(parts) < 2:
            continue
        status = parts[0][0]  # A / M / D / R / C...
        if status in ("R", "C"):
            # A rename copies+deletes: model it as a deletion of the source
            # (immutability checks) and an addition of the destination.
            if len(parts) >= 3:
                files.append(("D", parts[1]))
                files.append(("A", parts[2]))
            continue
        files.append((status, parts[1]))
    return files


def _regenerated_equals(repo: str, labels: str) -> bool | None:
    """True when the worktree CHANGELOG.md is byte-identical to what
    scripts/gen_changelog.dart --write-changelog produces from the same
    entries+archive inputs (run in a TEMP dir — the checkout is never
    mutated). None when dart is unavailable (skip with a warning)."""
    dart = shutil.which("dart")
    if dart is None:
        print("::warning::dart not on PATH — skipping the changelog "
              "regeneration equality check (the ci.yml static job runs it)")
        return None
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="cl-regen-")
    try:
        for sub in ("changelog/entries", "changelog/archive"):
            src = os.path.join(repo, sub)
            if os.path.isdir(src):
                shutil.copytree(src, os.path.join(tmp, sub))
        gen = subprocess.run(
            [dart, os.path.join(repo, "scripts", "gen_changelog.dart"),
             "--write-changelog"],
            cwd=tmp, capture_output=True, text=True,
        )
        if gen.returncode != 0:
            print(f"::error::changelog regeneration failed — the committed "
                  f"CHANGELOG.md cannot be generator-made\n{gen.stdout}"
                  f"{gen.stderr}")
            return False
        made = open(os.path.join(tmp, "CHANGELOG.md"), "rb").read()
        have = open(os.path.join(repo, "CHANGELOG.md"), "rb").read()
        return made == have
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

arguments.content:
### What changed
- Changelog becomes per-entry files: every PR adds its own
  `changelog/entries/<issue-or-pr>-<slug>.md` (YAML frontmatter
  `type`/`scope`/`issue` + 1–3 user-facing bullets) — parallel changes
  never touch a shared file, so changelog merge conflicts are gone by
  construction.
- New `scripts/gen_changelog.dart` aggregates the pending entries
  (`--stdout` flat release-notes body, `--group-by-type`, `--validate`,
  `--write-changelog`); `scripts/release_notes.sh` gains a new preference
  level: curated `## <version>` → **entries aggregate** → legacy curated
  `## Unreleased` → conventional commits. A broken entry fails the release
  notes loudly instead of shipping silently missing content.
- `CHANGELOG.md` (was 2814 lines) is now a ~70-line GENERATED index
  (preamble + `## Unreleased` + archive index); the 41 version sections
  moved to `changelog/archive/<version>.md` and the retired 2400-line
  curated Unreleased body (which rode releases 1.0.552+ verbatim, the
  gh-2337 131k class) to `changelog/archive/legacy-unreleased.md`.
- New CI guard `scripts/check_changelog_entry.py` (ci.yml `static` job):
  requires every PR to add an entry file (or carry `no-changelog`);
  CHANGELOG.md edits must be byte-identical to the regenerated output;
  rewriting/deleting archive history fails (additions — migration and
  entry housekeeping — stay allowed).

### Key decisions
- Pending-set rule mirrors the old flow exactly: ALL entry files
  aggregate into Unreleased until the tag cuts; no git-tag graph
  dependence, so shallow checkouts stay correct. Consumed-entry
  housekeeping is a conflict-free one-file PR.
- Flat aggregate output keeps byte-level shape parity with the old
  curated body (AC2 golden + old-vs-new parity test pin it); grouped
  rendering is opt-in.
- Rework dedupe: entries sharing an `issue:` keep the LAST file in
  (numeric-prefix, filename) order; the dropped one is reported.
- The release train needs no new wiring: `release_notes.sh` is the single
  notes source for the lazy draft, the stamper and the app workflows, and
  the stage-time fold (gh-1522) is untouched — verified by the CI stamp
  rehearsal on a staged tree (pubspec stamp + section from entries +
  pub.dev cap + `publish --dry-run` all green).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/changelog_gen_test.dart \
          test/release_notes_entries_test.dart \
          test/ci_changelog_entry_guard_test.dart \
          test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart
python3 scripts/check_changelog_entry.py --self-test
dart test --exclude-tags integration   # canonical core gate
```

Note for reviewers: `test/hub/local_hub_test.dart` had two escaped
`\${Directory.systemTemp.path}` literals that made the full suite create a
literal-named directory in the repo root (the gh-2185 template class,
re-found by the root allow-list gate); fixed to real temp paths.

<details><summary>Release-notes preference flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  PR[PR adds changelog/entries/<issue>-<slug>.md] --> GEN[gen_changelog.dart]
  GEN --> NOTES[release_notes.sh]
  CURATED[curated ## version section] --> NOTES
  NOTES --> BODY[release body: entries aggregate]
  NOTES --> STAMP[stamp_staged_release.sh folds into the staged tag section]
  GUARD[CI: entry added? CHANGELOG byte-equal to regenerated? archive immutable?] --> MERGE[merge — no shared-file conflicts]
end
```

</details>
